featured_reviews.name: Aditya Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Satkar Sweets and Snacks and was deeply disappointed by my experience, primarily due to severe hygiene and mismanagement issues.

Upon entering, we noticed Deepu, the staff member assigned to our order of garlic bread with corn, brooming the shop. While cleanliness is crucial in any food establishment, it was concerning to see him transition directly from sweeping the floor to food preparation without proper sanitation protocols.

Despite washing his hands post-brooming, Deepu proceeded to make our order without wearing gloves. When we requested that he put on gloves, he showed utter disappointment, which was both unprofessional and troubling. He placed the bread in his hand and then, with the other hand, began scooping cheese from a container, exposing our food to potential contamination.

When we asked to cancel our order and requested a refund, the staff reacted poorly, creating a scene rather than addressing our concerns professionally. This escalated further when my mother approached the owner for assistance. Instead of offering a solution, he disrespected her, which added to our frustration.

The overall experience at Satkar Sweets and Snacks was marred by inadequate hygiene practices and unprofessional behavior. It’s crucial for any eatery to prioritize cleanliness and customer service, and unfortunately, this establishment fell short in both areas. I cannot recommend Satkar Sweets and Snacks based on this experience.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Madaye
featured_reviews.review_text:
When it comes to Mulund, there is hardly anyone who is unaware about Hari Om Dry Fruits and Sweets. This popular spot boasts three locations in Mulund East, in addition to other outlets. Hari Om, a pure vegetarian restaurant, is conveniently situated at Hanuman Chowk, just a 5-minute walk from Mulund Railway Station.
On the ground floor, you can explore a variety of options including dry fruits, sweets, chat counters, and other packaged snacks. They also stock a wide range of international products. Don't miss their dahi Wada, pani puri, mini Chinese samosa, veg cheese Schezwan noodle frankie, and dabeli.
The restaurant itself is located on the first floor, featuring a bright and cool ambiance. It's an ideal family dining spot. Their menu offers a diverse selection of mocktails, pasta, pav bhaji, soups, noodles, tandoor items, rice dishes, and sizzlers. We sampled a variety of dishes and every one of them was delicious. The food is not overly spicy and has a great taste. The mocktails were particularly impressive. Even at around 10:30 PM, the service was exceptionally fast.
Additionally, they have one or two small halls that can accommodate groups of nearly 20 to 30 people for celebrations.
Overall, Hari Om is a fantastic restaurant that deserves a big thumbs up.

We recently visited Prasad Sweets to try their Kesar Basundi and Gulab Jamun, but the experience was quite disappointing. The server took an unusually long time just to take our order, and when it finally arrived, it was handed over in a plastic cover instead of a proper container.

The Kesar Basundi didn’t resemble basundi at all — it was more like plain milk, and the Gulab Jamun was slightly smashed. For a reputed sweet shop like Prasad, such presentation and service are really unexpected.

Basic hygiene and customer service standards were completely ignored, and the staff’s behavior was rude and indifferent. I truly hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves their service quality and hygiene practices.

featured_reviews.name: Mahadev G
featured_reviews.review_text:
We have been their regular customers for many years, but the quality and behavior have drastically gone down. The staff's manners are robotic, as if they're being scolded. The owner seems to believe in arguing with customers, which is laughable.
Yesterday, I went to place an order for our home's Haldi Kumkum program, and the guy said the samosa cost had increased due to the packing box. I wondered where this guy is living – is there no margin on their sweets? I think all their items are highly overpriced compared to their quality.
I placed the order because Prashant Sweets or Gaurav Sweets were far from Shree Nagar. I asked if I could pay 50% now via G-pay and 50% tomorrow via card, but they insisted on full payment. After realizing I'm a regular customer (as if I was buying things invisibly from their shop 😀), the lady said I could pay the remaining amount tomorrow via cash, UPI, or credit card.
Today, January 22nd, 2026, I went to collect my order, and they took 30 minutes to hand it over. On top of that, the owner's son said they have stopped payment through credit cards due to taxes.
Where is the Government of India? Where is the Income Tax Department? Are they all sleeping? These people just don't know how to behave with customers and are running a business. My appeal to all customers is: don't buy blindly from here. Observe their behavior and their staff's behavior – you'll realize you're living in the 18th century." 😊
Google should start adding --ve marking or red flag on the top of such small scale business outlets.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting Shree Bajrang Sweets and was thoroughly impressed by the quality and variety of their offerings. The Bengali sweets were outstanding, and the Rose Barfi and Blueberry Barfi were particularly delightful and flavorful.

The Mango Barfi, while a bit on the sweeter side, was still enjoyable, especially for those with a sweet tooth. The Mango Lassi was refreshing and perfectly balanced, making it a great companion to the sweets.

The Rose Kaju Katli was simply amazing, with a delicate rose flavor that complemented the rich, nutty taste. The Gud Kaju Katli was also a hit, offering a unique twist on the classic sweet. Lastly, the Mango Roll was both sweet and tasty, rounding out a wonderful experience at Shree Bajrang Sweets. If you're in the mood for delicious and well-crafted sweets, this place is definitely worth a visit!
